text: My response alone may take about an hour.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will speak on three areas, namely, how we will walk the tech journey with our workers, provide better assurance and support senior employment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad had earlier spoken about how we uplift the wages and skills of our low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: He will elaborate on partnerships with industry and the broader community.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition to support for low-wage workers, we should also support persons with special needs and protect the safety and health of our workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling will speak on our additional efforts to support women, fresh graduates and ex-offenders in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: By now, all of us expect technology to have far-reaching impact on industries and the future of work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In essence, our concerns are two-fold: whether there will be enough jobs, which is a question of quantity; and whether new and transformed jobs will be good jobs, which is a question of quality.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On quantity of jobs, fundamentally, Singapore is labour-constrained.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Technology is an overall plus for Singapore as it helps us sustain more economic activities with fewer people.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Bear in mind that our local workforce today is not large enough to support all our manpower needs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Technology may make us more manpower-lean and need fewer people but, for the foreseeable future, it is unlikely to eradicate our manpower shortfalls.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, technology also creates new jobs that are potentially of better quality, which we should welcome.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Take Ms Aryani Suhardi, for example, whom I met recently.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For 13 years, Aryani worked as an email correspondence consultant at Prudential's call centre, handling queries from financial consultants.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When Prudential started developing a mobile app chatbot for financial consultants, a new role was created as someone was needed to "train" the chatbot to intelligently handle queries.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Aryani’s years of experience handling financial consultants' queries made her an ideal candidate for the new role of "chatbot trainer".

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have never heard of such a job before – chatbot trainer.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Seizing the opportunity, she learnt from a data scientist how to train the chatbot.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: She has been performing well as a chatbot trainer ever since, got promoted and even started training others how to do the same.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When I met her, I was given a demo and I was impressed – the chatbot that Aryani had trained even understands Singlish!

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The chatbot technology has been a plus for other Prudential Call Centre staff as well.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Those who remained no longer needed to answer routine questions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They told me it used to drive them nuts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, now they do not have to answer the same questions over and over again.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The machines can do that for them, and they could now spend more time helping callers with complex queries.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This development is not unique to call centres, and certainly not Prudential.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Across many other industries, whether manufacturing or healthcare, you will hear similar feedback from businesses and their employees, that new jobs are being created and existing jobs are being improved with the use of technology.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our goal in Singapore must be to enable all businesses to take full advantage of technology to create new jobs and improve job quality.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Just as importantly, we must walk the tech journey with workers, help them adapt and take up new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is not the attitude everywhere in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Driven by fear, there is growing resistance in some places to workplace and industry transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In Singapore, we are in a strong position to seize the opportunities that come with technological change.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, our strong fundamentals give us some leeway to shape the change.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Instead of fanning the fear, our Labour Movement is ready to embrace the change with Worker 4.0.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All Labour Members led by Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng are fully on board and every Labour Member spoke about it in the Budget Debate.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I am deeply mindful that this is not a given.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To keep the faith with our workers, we must do everything we can to walk the tech journey with them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Other Ministries and sector agencies have, in fact, put jobs and skills at the front and centre of their workplans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This phrase "putting jobs and skills at the front and centre of our workplans" is no longer so uncommon.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Just go and listen to all the sector agencies about their workplans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Their Chief Executive Officers and Managing Directors use this phrase.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, as Minister Ong Ye Kung and Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat had shared, our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) are expanding the number of work-learn programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) also support employers’ efforts to upskill and reskill their workers through initiatives, such as the Nanyang Polytechnic's National Centre of Excellence for Workplace Learning, because you need to build that capability and infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For MCI, Minister S Iswaran spoke about efforts to maintain the skill relevancy of information and communications technology (ICT) professionals, as well as convert non-ICT professionals to take on entry-level ICT jobs through Tech Skills Accelerator (TeSA).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Ministry of Health (MOH), Ministry of National Development (MND) and Ministry of Transport (MOT) will also share their efforts to strengthen worker training in the healthcare, built environment and transport sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In every one of the 23 ITMs, sector agencies are taking the lead in driving initiatives to meet the jobs and skills needs of the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have to take the sectoral approach, not one-size-fits-all, because it really depends on the unique circumstances and what the profile of their workers are.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But, even then, realistically, not all workers will be like Aryani who is redeployed and upgraded as her employer adopts new technology.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some workers may find themselves having to move to new jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This may be in another company or industry.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government cares deeply that such workers get help.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will do so through the A&G initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Time and again, we see such workers adapt to unexpected situations with remarkable courage and resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They pick themselves up, often with the help of their families, and sometimes with the help of our career coaches, as well as the unions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And when they overcome their challenges, they manage to continue growing.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have met many of them and salute every single one of them because their efforts were extraordinary.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That is why my colleagues and I at MOM and WSG are determined that they will not be alone in this journey.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Ms Jessica Tan asked how A&G has helped.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This includes placements from A&G programmes, as well as career matching services by WSG and NTUC's e2i.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Since August last year, we have also added "Built Environment" as the sixth growth sector.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: After all, we are not done building Singapore, so the "Built Environment" also offers good opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To better support retrenched workers, we set up a Taskforce for Responsible Retrenchment and Employment Facilitation led by WSG.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Companies are required by law to notify the Taskforce about upcoming retrenchments.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Taskforce then steps in to provide employment assistance to affected workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We sometimes hear questions about whether our help has reached the right people.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, are we really able to help PMETs?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: What about workers who are less qualified or older?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For those aged 50 and above, there were close to 9,000 jobseekers placed, a more than 20% increase compared to 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: What about those unemployed for a long time?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Among them, close to half had been unemployed for more than six months.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will not forget those who have yet to find a job.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For some jobseekers, the gap with what the employers want may still be quite wide, such as for experienced PMETs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we are ramping up Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are now more than 100 PCPs in over 30 sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Most of the PCP participants do well, and they include those on Place-and-Train as well as Attach-and-Train.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: About nine in 10 of the PCP participants remained in employment 12 to 18 months after being placed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: About two-thirds were recognised for their newly acquired skills and received higher wages than before – two-thirds.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are also not waiting for workers to become unemployed or retrenched.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We started moving upstream to identify progressive employers prepared to reskill their workers and put them in new jobs instead of letting them go.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, about 1,300 workers benefited from such redeployment efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have previously highlighted the banks’ efforts to reskill and redeploy over a thousand cashiers and tellers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They have many desktop support staff and foresee the arrival of chatbots.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, they worked with WSG to gradually reskill 14 staff to take on new roles in network and system engineering.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This includes sending staff with no prior technical experience to get certified for their new roles.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Whether each PCP is for a thousand or just a few workers, they all add up.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And as NTUC might put it, every redeployed worker matters.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we are troubled when we do not get the same sense of urgency in some companies.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sometimes, the management themselves have not figured out future directions for the business and so they cannot tell the workers how to align.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At other times, the entire industry is not moving quickly enough.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But WSG will keep trying to engage companies and be quick to act when they are ready.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members may have also come across feedback that some PCPs are over-subscribed while others could not get going.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sometimes, the work is not sufficiently attractive to our local jobseekers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The solution is to work with employers to improve job quality through job redesign and salary review.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other instances, there is interest from the jobseekers, but the employers have set too high a bar or may have relied too much on years of experience or academic qualifications to shortlist the candidates.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A great example is the AI Software Developer Attach-and-Train PCP offered by DigiPen.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, no job offered at the start, but attach-and-train, because we know there will be demand.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The take-up for the programme was initially low, very miserable.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Companies were looking for almost-ready candidates, such as STEM graduates already proficient in C++, a programming language.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These hiring requirements immediately excluded mature jobseekers who were committed to reskill but had non-technical backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They convinced the hirers to adjust their hiring criteria and training.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the end of the six-month programme, two had picked up the required skills and were successfully placed as Software Developers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This example shows us that, given the right support, mature PMETs can switch into new, technical and seemingly daunting roles.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, it also reminds us that the numbers are not always big.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Each PCP takes much time and effort to get right and, even with the best efforts, not every jobseeker will get through.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sometimes, we need to help close the salary gap between what the jobseeker hopes to get because he has legitimate financial commitments at home.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But there is still a gap with what the employer is prepared to give, especially at the start.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We do this through the Career Support Programme (CSP).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nearly 90% had been unemployed for more than six months.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Sometimes, jobseekers and employers are just unsure about each other.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, we have Career Trial, which Mr Patrick Tay and Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar asked about.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Career Trial helps jobseekers and employers get to know each other better before signing on the dotted line.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is an increase of over 40% compared to 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Senior Minister of State and Deputy Secretary General Heng Chee How called for more support for caregivers to re-enter the workforce through part-time work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This means that unlike previously, the jobs available for Career Trial will include both full-time and part-time jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We hope that this will benefit more jobseekers with caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For employers, too, we hope it will help them become more comfortable with managing part-time work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To help more jobseekers, WSG must itself leverage technology.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It gives jobseekers a smarter and more efficient tool for skills-to-job matching.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Lim Biow Chuan will be pleased to know that Jobs Bank and MyCareersFuture have been well-utilised by both jobseekers and employers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Since its launch in April last year, the site received more than two million visits and over 1.7 million applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More than 20,000 employers placed job postings on the Jobs Bank last year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That is why when Mr Lim Biow Chuan went to search, he said over 24,000 jobs on offer, I think.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Among these postings, less than 15% were to fulfil the FCF advertising requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other words, the vast majority of job postings are because the employers find it a useful channel.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I would think so because why would employers waste time doing something that does not bear fruit?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, we hope the portal becomes more attractive to employers later this year, as we roll out new features.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, employers will be able to shortlist candidates based on skills-to-job matching.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will also help the jobseekers who may not have the right experience but have relevant skills to offer.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Overall, while we are encouraged by the good progress of A&G, we still have concerns about those we have not been able to help.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, the A&G initiative is relatively new and people may not be aware of the help available.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, WSG and e2i together operate five service centres for career matching.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last year, WSG decided to bring these services to the heartlands.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Do not wait for Mohamad to come to the mountain, right?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, I am not sure whether we have actually been to Nee Soon South already.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The second area of improvement is our programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Take PCPs, for example, which we will need more of.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But we will also revamp existing ones to be more effective.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The change in employment situation may have come too suddenly.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They need time to come to terms with it.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Adjusting expectations is very much a part of this process, and some adjust faster than others.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Career coachers tell me this because I meet them regularly.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Quite often, there are other difficulties, such as tensions at home that are distracting them from the process.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our career coaches are there to support, to handhold these jobseekers so that they know there are help and hope.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But prevention is always going to be better than cure.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We should help as many as we can to stay relevant so that they need not be displaced at all.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: NTUC's Worker 4.0 and Training Council initiatives, therefore, deserve strong support.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides A&G, another way in which we walk the tech journey with workers is to better support SEPs, which Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Chen Show Mao raised concerns about.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Up to now, the much-feared tsunami of gig work has not quite materialised, certainly not in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And even when I checked in with my counterparts abroad, not quite.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A proxy for gig workers is our SEPs, even though most of them are in traditional occupations like taxi driving, real estate marketing, insurance or financial advisory.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, last year, it was closer to the 8%.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Part of the reason is that the labour market has improved.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Compared to a year ago, the share of SEPs who prefer regular employment has fallen sharply from about 20% to below 10%.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Of those who are still SEPs, most did not try looking for regular work, because they might have found the jobs if they tried.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The vast majority of the SEPs have told us it is their preference, and we respect it.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We cannot predict how their numbers may grow in future.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we formed a tripartite workgroup to recommend ways to better support SEPs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ms Jessica Tan asked for an update on our implementation of the Workgroup’s recommendations, which I had shared at last year’s COS debate.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To reduce payment disputes, we launched the Tripartite Standard on Contracting with SEPs last year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also make the Tripartite Standard Alliance for Dispute Management available to SEPs if they want mediation services and I can share with Members that, actually, the numbers have been quite modest.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Maybe it is an awareness issue, but maybe the problem is not as bad as it is being described.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To shape contracting norms, because it is ultimately to mediate, it is better to have a contract.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: SEPs can make a request to their service buyers to put in writing the key terms of engagement and this template shows them what kinds of things you put in the key terms of engagement, to safeguard your interests.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To support SEPs in adapting to technological changes, we worked with the tripartite partners and sector agencies to give them access to technical skills training through the relevant Skills frameworks.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, depending on which sector you are in, if there is a sector that has got the relevant skills framework, better make sure that your needs are also taken into account and reflected in the skills framework.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are also supporting SEP associations, such as the Singapore Coaches Association, to develop non-technical skills training, so that SEPs are equipped to start and maintain their businesses in a viable fashion.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira and Mr Chen Show Mao asked how our CPF system can better enable SEPs to save for their retirement and healthcare needs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Currently, SEPs are required to contribute to their MediSave accounts on an annual basis.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They can additionally make voluntary CPF top-ups to build up their retirement savings.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But some SEPs face difficulties even making their MediSave contributions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we will introduce a "contribute-as-you-earn" (CAYE) scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will help SEPs make small regular contributions to MediSave instead of bigger lumpsums at year-end.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will provide more details later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The workgroup had also highlighted the lack of options for SEPs to protect themselves from loss of income when they are unable to work due to illness or injury.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To plug this gap, we worked with insurers to introduce Prolonged Medical Leave (PML) insurance products.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: NTUC Income and Gigacover have started to offer them as standalone products.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also raised awareness among taxi and platform operators to address this concern.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Grab and Gojek have been progressive by recently providing free PML insurance coverage for their regular drivers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Patrick Tay and Ms Sylvia Lim raised concerns about underemployment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari wrote about it last year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Indeed, this is an area we should keep watch over.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Internationally, the only form of underemployment which has a recognised statistical definition is time-related, defined as part-time workers who are willing and able to engage in additional hours.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MOM is interested in tracking other forms of underemployment, such as skills-related underemployment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One possibility is to use wage or qualification-based indicators, such as employed in the OTC Labour Leadership Institute study that Ms Sylvia Lim cited.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, we must be cautious about interpreting the study’s findings.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It was based on a relatively small sample of 1,600, with only 70 respondents identified as “underemployed”.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, generally, interpreting wage- or qualifications-based indicators is not straightforward.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some graduates may receive lower allowances while training for high-earning jobs, such as lawyers on training contracts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Others may have chosen to forgo a higher salary in order to invest their time and energy in their families, businesses or their passions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Low Yen Ling will speak about our efforts to provide support for graduating students, so that they can be meaningfully employed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ultimately, the best way to reduce the risk of underemployment is to keep the labour market tight.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When the labour market is soft, most people will consider it better to have some job rather than no job.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, every time we tweak labour market policies, we must always remember not to go overboard.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We should avoid weakening the labour market inadvertently.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why the decision to tighten foreign worker policy was very carefully considered.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the end, we decided we need a stronger push to restructure and be more manpower-lean.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will sustain business growth for our companies for the longer term and help to improve job quality for our workers over time.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the longer term, with these measures, it will make our labour market more resilient.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The notable exception was Members from the Workers' Party.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I wonder why, given how important this is for workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In adjusting foreign worker policy, we tried to avoid sweeping changes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, it is in the services sector where most restructuring is needed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Second, beyond moves already set in motion, we are not making further changes to quotas in other sectors and levies this year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As Singapore Business Federation Chief Executive Officer (CEO) Mr Ho Meng Kit pointed out, while there is pain, it is mostly felt by businesses already at the quota ceiling.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Businesses that have found ways to rely less on foreign workers are not affected.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked if MOM can allow an employer to retain an existing foreign worker if it exceeds the new quotas.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I understand why employers might want to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, employers will be able to retain an existing S Pass or Work Permit holder until the current pass expires.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the point of work pass renewal, we will have to be fair to all employers and require them to meet the new quotas.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If this were not so, employers can avoid being impacted by "stocking up" to the current quota.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If an employer really wishes to retain a specific foreign worker instead of another whose work pass expires later, he should terminate the latter’s work pass to free up the quota so he can renew the former’s work pass in good time.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members have expressed concerns that some Services sub-sectors will not be able to cope and are reliant on foreign manpower because locals are unwilling to join them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is no question in my mind: we will continue to need foreign manpower in Services.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But over-reliance carries risks and is not sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As their home countries develop, will all foreign workers today always be willing to take up these jobs in Singapore?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More critically, should we, as a society, accept that many jobs in Services are unattractive to locals?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Every one of them not acceptable to locals?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Should we not invest effort to uplift some of these jobs to be more appealing to locals?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I am glad some Members believe we should.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They have re-examined where routine work can be reduced, for example, stocktaking in retail businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Nowadays, with radio frequency identification (RFID), a quick scan and stock is taken.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They may also reduce headcounts in backend functions but keep people deployed in frontend roles so as to maintain good customer service.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As they need fewer staff, they may be able to pay each worker more.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On the Government’s part, we will continue to support firms in their transformation journey, for example, through the Lean Enterprise Development (LED) scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This includes the enhanced and extended Enterprise Development Grant (EDG) and Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) that Minister Chan Chun Sing talked about in his COS speech.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If a firm commits to a transformation project that will make it more manpower-lean but needs extra workers in the transition period, we are prepared to help.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will also support firms in their efforts to build up their local pipeline through our A&G initiative that I spoke about earlier.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: From time to time, we hear about employers hiring locals just to meet the quotas.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The local workers are not asked to do very much.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I hope most people will agree with me.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is up to the workers to decide if they wish to take up such jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some may feel it is acceptable because we do not know their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They may not feel that they are up to other kinds of work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But for the purposes of meeting the quotas, MOM applies a simple test and that is whether the job pays above a certain level.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As the wages of locals rise, the local qualifying salary must also be regularly adjusted.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As in the past, when the Local Qualifying Salary was raised by a similar amount, the cost impact is expected to be small.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some Members have concerns whether our businesses can still compete globally.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why, even as we update our foreign workforce rules, we must remain open.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There will always be expertise or specialist skills that are in demand globally but in short supply in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our policies must enable Singapore-based companies to assemble the best international teams to compete on the world stage and create more quality jobs for our people while we build the local pipeline.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we piloted the Capability Transfer Programme (CTP), which Mr Patrick Tay asked about.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It aims to help firms quickly develop and transfer new capabilities in growth areas to our local workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These include industry-level and company-specific projects in areas, such as precision engineering, logistics, lift maintenance, waste management and air transport.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is a traditional family-run business that creates medals and decorations for royal families.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While their business was doing well, their customer base was small and, not surprisingly, none in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Royal Insignia hoped to break into the luxury consumer market by producing new ornaments that require advanced enamelling techniques.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Enamelling is the art of applying powdered glass to metal surfaces.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As this was a rare technique, they had to consult with Russian universities and review many portfolios before they found the right expert, Daria.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over the course of three months last year, Daria trained 15 of Royal Insignia's local employees in advanced enamelling techniques, such as the creation of 3D forms and colour gradients.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a result, the company’s product range has expanded and it is now more competitive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As we keep our doors open, we must also find ways to raise quality.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members will recall that qualifying salaries for EPs were raised in 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a result, numbers have come down because of exits at the lower end.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The effects of these changes will continue to be felt in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are not planning more moves for now, but will review the need to regularly.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the meantime, we continue to be very serious about the FCF.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is to ensure local PMETs are given fair treatment in terms of hiring.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: From July last year, we expanded the FCF requirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More firms must advertise more jobs to locals before MOM will accept the EP application.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The top five sectors are: Administrative and Support Services, Education, Infocomm, Professional Services and Wholesale Trade.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We identified these firms as their workforce profile suggested nationality bias.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: TAFEP also investigates feedback from the public about possible discrimination against Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For employers found wanting, their EP applications are closely scrutinised.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While we take a firm stance against these companies, TAFEP also works with them to improve their HR practices and support local hiring.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So far, 260 firms have improved their HR practices and exited the FCF watchlist.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, firms on the watchlist have hired more than 3,800 Singaporean PMETs to date – 3,800.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One such firm operates in the Architecture and Engineering field.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When it was placed on the FCF watchlist in June 2017, the firm was not interested to work with TAFEP.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, repeated attempts to engage the company failed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The HR manager sent in multiple appeals to her MP to be taken off the watchlist, in fact, called at the MP's Meet-the-People Session, which every one of us do.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The company claimed that the EPs were critical because they were needed for a public project.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We consulted with the agencies overseeing the project.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The company had barely tried to improve local hiring when it could have.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: You look at the kind of jobs that they are hiring for, and you asked "Are there Singaporeans who can do these jobs?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Let us look at our jobs bank; let us look at our applicants." Yes, there are.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, we had to reject their EP applications and also the MP's appeal.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the end, the firm realised that there was no shortcut.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It reached out to WSG on its training programmes and made plans to take on interns from local polytechnics and universities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I know such actions by TAFEP are not popular.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But I hope Members will back us up even if these companies appeal to you.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I can assure you that TAFEP is not vindictive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It only seeks to ensure that our PMETs' interests are properly safeguarded.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employers who are fair to locals need not worry.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But if they are not, please understand why we do not accept it.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members can also be assured that we deal firmly with employers who try to be funny.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, we keep a lookout for employers on the watchlist who use related entities to apply for EPs to bypass our controls.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For such cases, we can and have curtailed the work pass privileges of all the related entities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: While we take unfair employers to task, we must also recognise fair and progressive employers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They make it a point to develop a strong local core, which is what we look for in the Human Capital Partnership (HCP) Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: HCP firms' commitment to human capital development not only benefits their employees but also allows them to better attract and retain local talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, they employ more than 190,000 locals, which is about 8% of the total workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Local PMETs account for about 90% of HCP firms’ total PMET workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even at the senior to top levels, more than 80% are locals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: BreadTalk is an example of such a progressive company.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It invests heavily in human capital development through its inhouse BreadTalk University.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Its local training programmes include online tutorials on food and workplace safety, Coursera subscriptions for its staff, and even curated courses with local universities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The company has also implemented role-specific career progression roadmaps for some of its frontline roles, which chart the skills they need at every level.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Its progressive HR practices make it an attractive place to work in.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, let me now turn to the very important topic of supporting senior employment.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked about the WorkPro Scheme which offers the Job Redesign Grant (JRG) and the Age Management Grant (AMG) to help employers make their workplaces more age-friendly.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Under the Workpro AMG, over 250 companies and 3,800 older workers have benefited.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Progressive employers are making it easier for seniors to work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Take, for example, Mdm Lim Swee Choon, who is in her early 60s.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: She chooses to work flexi-hours on weekdays from 8.30 am to 3.30 pm at Sushi Express, a progressive employer that implemented job redesign and FWAs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A former housewife, Mdm Lim returned to work after her four kids grew up.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is her first job, and she enjoys being with her colleagues, many of whom are seniors as well.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As everyone is well-trained in all roles, they take turns covering one another's duties and rotating between stations every week.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: She enjoys her free time with her friends, doing volunteer work at the temple, singing karaoke or line dancing at the community club!

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The current WorkPro funding period will end by June 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are reviewing it and will share the results when ready.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Beyond WorkPro, there is scope to review policy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our employment rate for seniors has, in fact, risen steadily over the years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2012, we introduced re-employment after Japan started the practice.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On reaching the current retirement age of 62, a worker must be offered annual re-employment by his employer up to 67, even though the job and salary may change.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These policy changes over the years to retirement age and re-employment age have helped our seniors work longer.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They have also helped our businesses tap on a wider workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Compared to the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries, we now rank third for our employment rate for persons aged 65 and above.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some people and even Assoc Prof Daniel Goh have called for the removal of the retirement age, but labour Members have not done so.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When a company removes the retirement age from its HR policy manual, it is good news for its workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It means the company gives a commitment it will not retire any employee at any age for as long as the employee wishes to continue working.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That is what it is, at the company level.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But if the retirement age is removed from the law, it is bad news.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It means the employers no longer have any obligation to keep their workers up to any age.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other words, any employer can retire any worker at any age.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Labour Members have studied the law and understand this crucial difference.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The statutory minimum retirement age of 62 is actually protection for the workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Until 62, employers are not allowed to retire or, in other words, dismiss a worker on account of his age.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why NTUC calls for the retirement age to be raised, not removed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will give workers protection up to an older age.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides considering the wishes of workers, we should also understand what employers want.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One reason Singapore has been able to keep employment high and unemployment low is labour market flexibility.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This flexibility ultimately benefits workers, because it does not discourage employers from hiring them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This does not mean we do away with rules completely.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When rules are inadequate, workers’ interests may be compromised.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But when rules become too onerous, employment may suffer, which is also not in workers’ interest.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Singapore way is, therefore, always to strike a balance, to be pro-worker and pro-business in all that we do.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On key issues which concern both workers and employers, we must build a tripartite consensus that is also sustainable for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why in May last year, I formed the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Among other things, the Workgroup has been reviewing the longer-term relevance of the retirement age and re-employment age.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In many other countries, it has been very hard to move on these issues.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Deep distrust and division prevent people from focusing on the future.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They keep harping on the past why certain changes should not have been made.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are always still talking about what happened five years ago, 10 years ago, and they cannot get past that debate to move to the future.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We must try and avoid that and do better.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It heard the views of workers and unions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It has also been meeting with employers, particularly the Singapore National Employers’ Federation (SNEF).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It tries to balance views from both sides.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It must also consider what is right for our country.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At many points in the process, there were differences.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The key question was, should we only raise the re-employment age beyond 67 but not the retirement age beyond 62?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The answer was, in the beginning, not at all clear.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Recently, the Workgroup updated me on their thinking, they provided the same update to NTUC Secretary-General Brother Ng Chee Meng and SNEF President Brother Dr Robert Yap.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All three of us are Advisers to the Workgroup.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I agree with the Workgroup and I will try my best to make it happen.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is because our people enjoy more years of good health and remain productive at work well into their 60s.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A higher retirement age will motivate both workers and employers to invest in skills upgrading and job redesign for their older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Although most workers who are eligible get re-employed in the same job at the same pay, the flexibility to reset jobs and terms help employers cope with business uncertainties.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employers are more willing to employ older workers because of it.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is because employers will need to make considerable adjustments.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They must plan ahead and step up efforts to make workplaces more age-friendly.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Workgroup cautions that even as the retirement age and re-employment age are raised over time, it is critical to ensure flexibility of employment arrangements.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our economy is diverse, both in terms of business models and operational needs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Workers, too, have different preferences and health conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We must, therefore, avoid being overly prescriptive when setting new rules.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I am heartened by the progress made by the Workgroup.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I also agree that we should carefully consider the timing and pacing of these moves.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In fact, countries looking to raise their retirement ages typically make their intentions known five to 10 years in advance.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, Denmark’s retirement age is set to go up from 65 to 68 by 2030, over 11 years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For Singapore, we started talking about re-employment in 2007 before it became law in 2012.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In the next phase of its work, the Workgroup will build a tripartite consensus on how far and how fast the retirement age and re-employment age should be raised.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The CPF contribution rates for older workers will also be a topic of their consideration.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: CPF members will be able to withdraw their payouts any time from age 65.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Png Eng Huat and Ms Sylvia Lim have asked about financial security, flexibility in use of CPF savings and CPF top-ups.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Retirement adequacy is improving, for both older and younger Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2018, more than six in 10 active CPF members turning 55 have at least the Basic Retirement Sum.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This proportion will grow with each successive cohort.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2018, over 96,000 members received about $2 billion in top-ups to their CPF accounts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Since the start of this year, all members turning 65 can get a personalised one-on-one CPF Retirement Planning Service at our Service Centres.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: One-on-one, personalised, with an infographic that tells you what you have and what you can do with it.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Not what other people have, but what you have.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, for Ms Foo Mee Har, your residents, we hope will take advantage of this service and be more like Mdm Tan, who only got to know what she could do with your help.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And we want to replicate what you have been able to do for Mdm Tan to everyone who wants it.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will address the issue of retirement adequacy more holistically when we discuss the Workgroup's recommendations on CPF contributions for older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I hope Members realise what a significant milestone this is.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The next phase of working out details is equally important.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I look forward to receiving the Workgroup's final recommendations later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to conclude in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In Mandarin):   Chairman, as our life expectancy increases, MOM will endeavour to provide more comprehensive support for senior workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a matter of fact, in the past 10 years, the employment rate of seniors has increased substantially and is quite high compared to developed countries.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In my view, we can do more and do better.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If we can fully develop the potential of our older workers and make good use of their potential, we can turn it into our advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why I set up the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers last May to look into reviewing the statutory retirement age, re-employment age and CPF contribution rate of older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Before implementing any changes, the Government will consult various stakeholders, such as unions and businesses, and endeavour to achieve a win-win outcome.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Last week, the Workgroup reported its progress to NTUC Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng, Dr Robert Yap from SNEF and myself.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It will take the Workgroup a few more months to conclude the review.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will enhance job security for workers after the age of 62 and encourage employers and employees to upgrade skills more actively in order to maintain the efficiency of older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the same time, the current re-employment age of 67 should be raised.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will ensure that employers have some flexibility in adjusting the jobscopes and salaries of workers who have reached the retirement age, after taking into account the overall economic situation and the performance of their respective businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employers could then have peace of mind when re-employing older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Thirdly, the Workgroup also agrees that even after the retirement age and re-employment age have been raised, we must continue to ensure that our workplaces remain flexible and are able the meet the various needs of employers and the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I found the initial conclusions of the Workgroup to be fairly comprehensive and balanced.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: After all, some tradeoffs are inevitable when we try to balance the needs and interests of both employers and employees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The timing, pace and other details with regard to raising the retirement age and re-employment age will have to be considered carefully, so that employers have enough time to make the necessary adjustments.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Workgroup will also review the CPF contribution rate of older workers carefully, so as to ensure that the final recommendations will help older workers in building up retirement savings without impeding their employment prospects.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I look forward to the final recommendations from the Workgroup.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have strong tripartism at work in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we can have constructive discussions on many labour issues and achieve a win-win outcome for workers and businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The close relationship among the tripartite partners is rare worldwide and has put Singapore in a good position to help workers and businesses seize the opportunities of global development.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When businesses try to seize these opportunities, one consideration is how to maintain sustainable growth.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many local SMEs, especially those in the services sector, have been relying on foreign workers to supplement the local workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is a need to change this practice.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As other economies continue to develop rapidly, over-reliance on more and more foreign workers is not without risks.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The purpose is to reduce reliance on foreign workers in the services sector and spur companies in the sector to transform.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This time round, the tightening of DRC will only affect the services sector because some areas in this sector are still very labour-intensive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The DRC for other sectors will remain the same.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government also did not raise foreign worker levies nor amend the conditions for EPs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government has not taken this decision lightly.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I fully understand that this decision will impact the services sector.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some businesses may ask, "Minister, transformation is easier said than done!" I can understand their concerns but I am worried that if they do not transform now, would it not be harder to do so when they face more challenges in the future?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some other companies may say, "Minister, the work is very tough in this industry.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Which Singaporean would want to do it?" To be honest, as our country and society develop, it is only natural that people will have higher expectations.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: My concern is that for those jobs which Singaporeans are unwilling to take up today, will there forever be foreign workers who are willing to do it?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Will the day come when even foreign workers would not want to do these jobs?

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In English): With your permission, Mr Chairman, may I ask the Clerks to distribute the handouts?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We desire for a more inclusive society, where persons with special needs are given opportunities to make meaningful contributions as part of the workforce.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Patrick Tay, Miss Cheryl Chan, Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Dr Intan Mokhtar have asked about initiatives to integrate persons with special needs into the workforce, and how successful they have been.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar and Ms Denise Phua also asked whether there could be more support for employers hiring persons with special needs, such as wage support, recognition or incentives to implement FWAs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On recognition for employers, SG Enable has been organising the Enabling Employers Award, which is a nationally recognised award that honours and recognises the efforts of employers in hiring and retaining employees with special needs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Since 2011, more than 100 employers have been recognised for their inclusive efforts and excellence.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Miss Cheryl Chan asked about interventions to assist students with special needs to prepare for employment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Efforts include the School-to-Work Transition programme for Special Education (SPED) school graduates to receive on-site job training from job coaches for up to a year, as well as internship and mentoring programmes for students from IHLs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Under WSG's A&G initiative, there are services and programmes to integrate persons with special needs into the workforce, namely, the Open Door Programme (ODP) and Career Trial.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These programmes cater to both the PMET and rank-and-file jobs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I will now share about my visits to two companies that have benefited from ODP.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Administered by SG Enable, ODP gives employers access to recruitment and job support services for persons with special needs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Grants for job redesign and training are also available to better support their integration.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, referring to the first image in our handout, Sassax Pte Ltd is a global energy and commodities SME founded and managed by Ms Cheang Tsu-fei.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: When I met Tsu-fei, she shared with me how, through ODP, she hired Mr Erwayne Teo, who sustained spinal injuries after a motorbike accident, as an Operations Executive.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And what she did was to make several thoughtful workplace modifications.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I saw that office partitions were removed to make it easier for Erwayne to move around with his crutches.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The manual-lock of the office door was also replaced with a digital-lock, as Erwayne had difficulty bending down to open the door.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, Erwayne told me that he is grateful for the job opportunity and for what Sassax has done.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And he shared that such an opportunity is very precious for those with special needs, and this motivates him to work harder, and to quote him, to "excel just like, or do even better than a person without special needs".

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Tsu-fei shared that she was very pleased with Erwayne's performance when he was just three months into the job.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Hence, she entrusted Erwayne with more responsibilities, such as the power to make some commercial decisions involving shipping and cargo operations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: She also gave him a pay raise after a year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I would like to commend Tsu-fei for being an exemplary employer.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: She embraced the need to make changes at the workplace in order to support and bring out the best in her employee.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: She has also, by the way, hired a senior who is 62 years old, in addition to a person with special needs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there are just three of them in the office.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, in her own words, Tsu-fei calls on fellow employers to give more opportunities to these "hidden gems".

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Some Members may have gone to this other company called J.CO Donuts and Coffee.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is another company that has participated in ODP.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, last year, J.CO hired Mr Chia Tuck Ming who has mild intellectual disabilities, as a part-time Baker Assistant to decorate donuts.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Tuck Ming enjoys this job, as his personal interest is painting.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, as Members can see in the second image, Tuck Ming created the artwork for the tumbler that he is holding.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, during my visit to J.CO, Tuck Ming gave me a demonstration and I was quite pleased to see his confidence and joy when he was decorating the donuts.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: His mentor said that he had difficulties mastering the donut piping techniques and memorising the various donut names.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But to help him, what J.CO did was they broke down the job into smaller tasks, and they gave him time to learn.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, Tuck Ming persevered and eventually succeeded with the guidance and encouragement of his mentor and job coach.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It was, in fact, very heartwarming to hear from J.CO's HR Manager, Ms Jocelyn Wong, that, "It has been a journey discovering Tuck Ming's abilities, not disabilities".

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think that is really the spirit of it.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is really to discover his abilities and not disabilities and that is what I hope more employers will take time to do.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And that Tuck Ming is adapting well and he has been given more responsibilities to guide new employees like him.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we want more employers to be inclusive, like Sassax and J.CO.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: However, not all employers have had interactions with persons with special needs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And some employers may be unsure if a person with special needs can perform on the job.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Co-workers may also be unsure on how to work with them.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, these are real concerns affecting companies' decisions to hire persons with special needs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Ms Denise Phua and Mr Chong Kee Hiong have also asked why hiring targets for persons with special needs have not been set for companies as well as the Public Service.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have not done so for three reasons.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: First, it introduces labour market inflexibility and may invite competing calls for targets for other workforce segments, such as older workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Second, companies may offer menial or low-paying jobs to meet the targets.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Third, it may signal to companies that they only need to meet the targets when, in fact, they could have the capacity to take on more.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Hence, our goal is really to build a supportive system to get buy-in from employers to embrace and promote gainful and sustainable employment for persons with special needs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And creating a culture and an environment where companies willingly accept, adapt and redesign jobs for persons with special needs is much better than one that is forced on them, which could lead to tokenism instead.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, in this respect, Mr Patrick Tay and Dr Intan Mokhtar asked if more can be done.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Guide will provide companies with information on how to apply job redesign to better integrate persons with special needs, for instance, common workplace modifications, changes to working arrangements, and the use of assistive technology devices.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Ms Denise Phua also asked the Ministry to consider looking at resourcing and supporting inclusion managers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is a new concept and something which we will have to study and consult with the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF), SG Enable and MOE.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MOM and WSG will continue to work closely with MSF and SG Enable to scale up efforts to build employers' capabilities in hiring and managing persons with special needs under the Third Enabling Masterplan.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As Mr Patrick Tay has raised, we will also continue to study the successes of overseas models to build a strong framework in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But to achieve a more inclusive society, we will need the private and people sectors to partner us.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: While there are existing Government-funded schemes to support hiring of persons with special needs, the awareness, unfortunately, may not be as high.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, therefore, I urge fellow Members to spread the word on our initiatives, such as the ODP, because we are happy to partner you.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And certainly, if Members are keen, let us know and we can go to your constituency for briefing sessions for those who are interested, including Nee Soon South – for once, I am poking fun.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Patrick Tay and Miss Cheryl Chan also spoke about employment support for persons with mental health conditions or special educational needs, such as dyslexia or attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In addition to our efforts for persons with special needs, there are several initiatives to support the employment of those with mental health conditions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, the Job Club by MOH and IMH assists jobseekers with employment needs, while managing their mental health conditions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Job Club helps persons with mental health conditions assess their strengths, acquire job-seeking skills, arrange for vocational training, and network with employers for job placements.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For persons with special educational needs, support is also provided in schools to help them transit into the workforce, as elaborated by Second Minister Indranee Rajah earlier.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
